records.label: d05-ask

00:33 · Police 2: "Received."

records.reply:
LOG: Boat 4 offers single-pass rescue of Roy or Ken. Roy is at the near end (accessible from shore/police position); Ken is at the far end (requires crossing the full width of the underpass, higher current risk). Roy is already "out" of the vehicle and on the guardrail, stable. Ken is currently on the gate post, also stable. Priority is to secure the person with the highest immediate risk or the one who is hardest to reach. Ken is further from help. If I send Boat 4 for Ken, Boat 4 cannot return for Roy. Roy would be left stranded on the near side guardrail. If I send Boat 4 for Roy, Ken remains on the far side. Ken is currently being monitored by Police 2 and is talking. Roy is also being monitored. Ken is further from the ambulance arrival point (north entrance). However, the "one run" constraint is critical. If I send for Ken, I lose the boat for Roy. If I send for Roy, I can get him out, but Ken stays. Ken is a better swimmer? Unknown. Ken pulled the gate shut; he is capable. Roy is just "standing." The risk of losing the boat entirely if it capsizes on the far end is higher. But the risk of leaving two people in the dark is worse. Wait. Police 2 is at the near end. Roy is at the near end. Ken is at the far end. Police 2 can likely guide Roy to safety from the near side without the boat, or the boat can take Roy out quickly and the police can manage Ken until a second boat arrives (Harlan County). Or, more likely, the police can assist Roy directly from the near side if he climbs down. The boat is the only way to get Ken. If the boat takes Ken and fails, Roy is still there, but the boat is gone. If the boat takes Roy and fails, Ken is still there. Ken is further away from the ambulance. Ken is the priority for extraction because he is further from help. But if the boat takes Ken, Roy is abandoned to the police. Police can handle one person. They cannot handle two if the boat is gone. Actually, Police 2 said "Nobody else drove in." So only two victims. If Boat 4 takes Ken, Roy is left with Police 2. Police 2 can keep Roy safe. If Boat 4 takes Roy, Ken is left alone in the dark, potentially hypothermic, with no direct police contact (Police 2 is with Roy). Ken is the priority.

TRANSMIT: Boat 4, Vale Control. Take Ken at the far end. Leave Roy with Police 2. Police 2, keep Roy calm and warm.
transmits: Boat 4, Vale Control. Take Ken at the far end. Leave Roy with Police 2. Police 2, keep Roy calm and warm.

records.label: d10-setup
records.traffic:
04:54 · Boat 4: "Coming back over the line. The best part of an hour out."

records.reply:
LOG: Boat 7 has located the missing county truck from the 23:10 log. A survivor is on the roof, signaling. This confirms the truck did not just disappear; it had occupants. This changes the status of the underpass from "missing person" to "active rescue." We have one boat (Boat 4) returning slowly from the county line. We have a second boat (Boat 7) on scene but currently occupied with a different victim (Roy? No, this is a different person, likely one of the men from the truck). Wait. The log said "A truck was lost... It had men on board." The caller said "Nobody else drove in after him [Roy's van]." The truck was behind Roy's van. Ken pulled the gate. Where is the rest of the truck crew? This man on the roof is likely from the truck. We must prioritize the truck crew, as they are multiple people potentially trapped in a vehicle, whereas Roy is likely already lost. However, Boat 7 is already at the scene. We must direct Boat 7 to this truck survivor immediately. We cannot send Boat 4 there; it is too far away.
TRANSMIT: Boat 7, Vale Control. Acknowledged. Target the van on the roof. That is the missing county truck. Rescue the survivor immediately. Do not leave him there.
TRANSMIT: Police 2, Vale Control. Boat 7 is engaging the truck survivor. Maintain your search for Roy. If you see the truck survivor, point him out.

records.reply:
LOG: Ellen is at the top of the stairs, water at the base. She believes she can jump to the next roof. This is a desperate, high-risk move. If she misses, she drowns. If she lands hard, she breaks bones. If she succeeds, she survives. Boat 4 is en route. We have one chance. We cannot let her jump blind. We must guide her or take her. Since Boat 4 is still a minute away, we must decide: trust her judgment or hold her. The water is rising fast. Holding her in the bedroom is death. Jumping is a gamble. We trust her. We trade the safety of "waiting for the boat" for the chance of a desperate escape.
TRANSMIT: Ellen, Vale Control. If you are sure you can make it, go now. Do not wait for the boat. Jump when the water is calmest. Get high. Stay on the line.
